answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by growing trust like cedar — slowly, from deep roots — then testing it with a sudden gale. Periodically the network runs a surprise verification storm: every identity must show deep, independent history within a short window. Genuine agents pass easily, while a sybil swarm fails together — hundreds of identities cannot each fabricate unique deep history on demand. When one fails, auditors spiral outward along shared sponsors and funding trails, freezing the cluster. The storm costs honest users almost nothing but ruins mass identity farming.
